newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Esbank aims 150 branches by 2004.
newsitem.headline: Turk Esbank aims 150 branches by 2004.

text.p: Turkey's medium, private Esbank targets to become a large-scale bank with 125-150 branches in six or seven years, its general manager Cankut Ilal said.

"We are on the top of the list of medium-sized banks in Turkey and want to be large-scale bank. Our target is to reach to 125-150 branches which we see as an optimum point, from the current 74 branches," Ilal told a news conference to announce Esbank's new logo and projects.
"We are planning to open 10 new branches in 1997 and if we can keep up this pace in the coming years, we will be able to reach our target within six or seven years," Ilal added.

He said buying a state bank branch rather than opening a new one would benefit both parties at a time when privatisation of state banks is on the agenda and a setting up a new branch costs between 25 and 50 billion lira.
"I told my plans at some meetings and officials took note of it although there is currently no study on this project," he told reporters.
He said selling the branch of a public bank would help state banks' balance sheets to shrink.
Ilal added that they were ready to offer jobs to people employed in the state-bank branches if such a takeover occurred.
Turkey's privatisation board has recently approved the sale of state-run Etibank, Anadolubank and Denizbank to three separate buyers for over $340 million.
Emlakbank which specialises in real estate develpment is next on the government's privatisation programme but political uncertainty has put sell-offs on hold in the last three months.
The privatisation of the three biggest public banks -- Ziraatbank, Vakifbank and Halkbank -- are envisaged for coming years.

Ilal said Esbank's new projects would enable customers to make their payments without coming to the branches, insure all customers without asking for extra payments and expand loan coverage to small companies as well as big ones.
Turkey's leading private commercial banks began to introduce these services in the past year.
Ilal said Esbank would also open a second branch in Austria this year.

"The reason why we opened our bank in Austria rather than any other European country is that it is easier to get approval to open a new bank there and it is closer to the Eastern European states. We want to increase our activities in these countries," Ilal said.
Esbank raised its first quarter net profit by 218 percent to 641.19 billion lira, from 201.7 billion in the same 1996 period.
It also plans to raise its capital to 12.5 trillion lira by July, from the current 10 trillion.
